items.title: The stacks section opens in your voice
items.my_version: I don't think there's one supplement stack that heals everyone's gut. Whatever you take, the order matters. Get your digestion working mechanically first, then reset your diet and your gut motility, and only go after bugs and parasites with antimicrobial or anti-parasite protocols if you still have symptoms after that.
items.before: I do not think there is a universal supplement stack that heals everyone's gut. The correct order still matters: fix digestion mechanics first, reset diet and motility, then only escalate into antimicrobial or anti-parasite protocols if symptoms persist.

items.title: The three things to look for: four versions read AI
items.your_version:
That said, some people want a ready-made stack rather than buying every ingredient for it separately. So, if I were to recommend a general “repair and rebuild” approach, it would be a stack that covers three categories:
First,  support the Microbiome with a well-tolerated probiotic or probiotic system. 
Then keep the probiotics well-fed with a good prebiotic, and take butyrate itself or something that helps short-chain fatty acid production, especially the main one, butyrate.
Other nutrients will help support barrier repair, such as glutamine, zinc carnosine, colostrum, mucosal-support herbs, or similar compounds

items.title: The kits, with your answer about them
items.my_version: Gemini suggested these kits to me, but so far they're the best ones I've seen, tho I haven't used them myself, so check the reviews. Designs for Health GI Revive is one of the more complete gut-lining repair formulas. You still need the rest of a gut protocol with it. There's also Dr. Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit, which makes sense if leaky gut is your main problem. Microbiome Labs Total Gut Restoration is the best general stack of these, because you get mucosal support along with the probiotic and prebiotic.
items.before: The best general commercial stack I have seen so far is Microbiome Labs Total Gut Restoration, because it combines probiotic, prebiotic, and mucosal-support components. For a more leaky-gut-specific stack, Dr. Ruscio's Leaky Gut Support Kit is a reasonable option. For a single gut-lining repair formula, Designs for Health GI Revive is one of the more complete products, but it should be understood as a repair product, not a complete gut protocol by itself.

items.title: The cleanse stacks, with your berberine note
items.my_version: I wouldn't start everyone off on the general "gut cleanse" stacks either, the ones built around oregano oil, wormwood, black walnut, berberine or other antimicrobial herbs. Those are for later (Phase 3), once you have more reason to suspect overgrowth, parasites, H. pylori or something else specific. (My own advice is different for H. pylori, where berberine works well: see Parasites, above.)
items.before: I would not recommend general "gut cleanse" stacks built around oregano oil, wormwood, black walnut, berberine, or other antimicrobial herbs as a universal starting point. Those belong later in the decision tree, when there is a stronger reason to suspect overgrowth, parasites, H. pylori, or another specific problem. (My own advice is different for H. pylori, where berberine works well: see Parasites, above.)

items.title: Start low, and who should see a clinician
items.my_version: Start with low doses, especially of prebiotics, resistant starch, butyrate-support products and probiotics. And if you have severe pain, GI bleeding, fever, dehydration, rapid weight loss, an active IBD flare, cancer, immune suppression, a pregnancy, or another complex medical condition, don't stack supplements on your own, work with a qualified clinician instead.
items.before: Start low, especially with prebiotics, resistant starch, butyrate-support products, and probiotics. People with severe pain, GI bleeding, fever, dehydration, rapid weight loss, active IBD flares, cancer, immune suppression, pregnancy, or complex medical conditions should work with a qualified clinician instead of self-stacking supplements.

items.my_version: Mitochondrial & Cellular Energy Starvation (Glutamine, Butyrate, TCA Intermediates): Your gut barrier requires massive amounts of immediate, localized energy to maintain tight junction integrity. If your enterocytes (small intestine) or colonocytes (large intestine) lack their preferred mitochondrial fuels, the barrier structurally collapses, allowing lipopolysaccharides (LPS) and endotoxins to leak into systemic circulation.
